document.title: Sixnine unified generation contract examples
notes: This file is not OpenAPI, an SDK, a fixture for production, or proof that an endpoint accepts these fields.
All identifiers, hashes, timestamps, prices and runtime fingerprints below are fictional examples.
Existing /v1 route paths are retained where applicable; normalized source_ref and richer status fields are proposed additions.
Authentication headers are deliberately omitted. Ownership always comes from the authenticated principal, never an owner_id supplied by a caller.
Public responses expose safe profile identifiers, not GPU addresses, provider credentials or executable workflows.

normalized_spec.scope: Proposed server-validated value object for a direct creation; not today's HTTP request schema

value.prompt: 纸船沿着浅溪缓缓向前，镜头贴近水面跟随，保留自然流水声。

server_resolves: Asset ownership, ready state, decoded metadata and authoritative hashes
Engine and model revisions, precision, frame sampling, defaults and hardware envelope
Source revision and operation identity; actor attribution
Capabilities, current admission policy and immutable effective request

preflight.scope: Proposed response additions to POST /v1/generation-plans; fictional admissible profile

estimate.meaning: Reservation is not the final user charge or measured GPU cost

invariants: Preflight does not rent a GPU or submit an inference.
A ready plan is not an inventory guarantee; confirmation rechecks authorization, source, expiry and budget atomically.
Quick Chat cards must use their existing preflight/submission path, not bypass revision uniqueness through this route.

submit.scope: Existing direct-job request shape, with proposed richer response projection
invariants: Network replay uses the same key and body and returns the same accepted operation.
A separate owner/resource/revision operation constraint prevents a browser and another Agent from duplicating the same generation decision.
The caller polls this job; it does not submit a new job because capacity is unavailable.

job_projections.scope: Partial proposed public GET /v1/jobs/{id} projections; retain other existing fields
invariants: These are separate observations of one hypothetical job, not three jobs.
Unknown submission is unresolved, not proof of failure or permission to resubmit.
A succeeded result requires output validation, durable storage and committed artifact metadata.
Output duration is measured from the actual artifact; equality to the example sampling duration is not a universal guarantee.

problem.scope: Proposed RFC 9457 error; adapt legacy consumers before changing media type or fields

response.title: 所选执行配置尚未开放此控制
response.detail: 草稿已保留；请选择已验收的兼容配方或移除此项后重新预检。

capability_entry.scope: Proposed per-profile capability entry; explicitly not enabled or verified

batch_semantics.scope: Proposed aggregate view; not a replacement for current Quick Chat Submission/Item or /v1/batches wire schemas
invariants: Retry selection contains only item_2_demo; item_1_demo stays successful and item_3_demo is reconciled.
An explicit user retry preserves the submission/item but creates a new execution and job, linked to the prior execution, matching the existing Quick Chat behavior.
Admission recovery and output collection recovery keep the original job; a platform technical retry uses a new attempt only under an explicit bounded policy.
A deliberate new draw is a new generation decision, not deletion of an idempotency record.

adapter_semantics.scope: Internal proposed protocol, not a public HTTP endpoint or confirmed native-engine feature
invariants: Persist attempt intent before the upstream side effect; persist receipts and evidence after it.
A local fence protects database ownership; it cannot alone prevent an old process making an upstream call.
Idempotent upstream submission or an appropriate gateway is required before promising safe automatic replay.
Provider resource creation is a separate Capacity Controller contract with separate intent and cost accounting.
